# HTTP Logs Receiver

The HTTP Logs Receiver is for ingesting HTTP logs and parsing the records received
based on the configured record type.

## Configuration

Example:

```yaml
receivers:
  httplogs:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4433
    encoding: awscloudwatchmetricstreams_encoding
    access_key: "some_access_key"
    tls:
      cert_file: server.crt
      key_file: server.key

extensions:
  awscloudwatchmetricstreams_encoding:
    format: json
```

The configuration includes the OpenTelemetry collector's server [confighttp](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/tree/main/config/confighttp#server-configuration),
which allows for a variety of settings. Only the most relevant ones will be discussed here, but all are available.

### endpoint:
The address:port to bind the listener to.

default: `localhost:4433`

See our [security best practices doc](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/security/config-best-practices/#protect-against-denial-of-service-attacks) to understand how to set the endpoint in different environments.

### tls:
See [documentation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/config/configtls/README.md#server-configuration) for more details.

A `cert_file` and `key_file` are required.

### encoding:

The ID of an [encoding extension](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/extension/encoding) for decoding logs or metrics.
This configuration also supports the built-in encodings listed in the [Encodings](#encodings) section.

If no encoding is specified, then the receiver will default to a signal-specific encoding: `cwmetrics` for metrics, and `cwlogs` for logs.
In the future, the default encodings will be removed, and it will be required to specify an encoding extension.

### record\_type:

Deprecated, use `encoding` instead. `record_type` will be removed in a future release; it is an alias for `encoding`.

### access\_key (Required):
The access key to be checked on each request received. This can be set when creating or updating the delivery stream.

### compression\_algorithms:

The allow-list of request body encodings accepted from the `Content-Encoding` header. The raw
body is decompressed with the named codec before it is handed to the decoder. The empty value,
`none`, and `identity` all select the plain body. Each entry must be one of `gzip`, `zstd`,
`zlib`, or `deflate`. By default the receiver accepts identity, `gzip`, `zstd`, `zlib`, and
`deflate`; setting `compression_algorithms` restricts the set to identity plus the listed codecs.

```yaml
receivers:
  httplogs:
    compression_algorithms: [ gzip, zstd ]
```

Requests whose `Content-Encoding` header is not on the allow-list are rejected with `400 Bad
Request` and no records are consumed.

### flush\_items:

The maximum number of decoded records a streaming decoder holds before forwarding a batch
downstream. `0` (the default) defers to the decoder's own default, which is `1000`. Must not be
negative.

### flush\_bytes:

The maximum number of decoded body bytes a streaming decoder holds before forwarding a batch
downstream. `0` (the default) defers to the decoder's own default, which is `1 MiB`. Must not be
negative.

`flush_items` and `flush_bytes` only take effect when the configured encoding exposes a
streaming decoder.

## File tracking

By default the receiver has no memory across requests: if a delivered file is resent, it is
processed from the beginning. File tracking makes deliveries of a file resumable: the last
successfully exported line of each file is recorded, and a resend of the same file skips the
already-exported prefix. A resend of a fully processed file is a no-op (`200 OK`, nothing
re-forwarded).

File tracking is **disabled by default** and only takes effect when both are true:

- `file_tracking.enabled: true`, and
- the request carries the delivered file's name in its `X-Common-Attributes` header under
  `file_attribute` (default `file.path`).

```yaml
receivers:
  httplogs:
    ...
    # Optional: a storage extension whose client persists the checkpoints.
    # With this set, checkpoints are shared across all replicas of the receiver.
    storage: internal/redis
    # Optional: enable per-file, per-line delivery tracking (default: disabled).
    file_tracking:
      enabled: true
      file_attribute: file.path    # X-Common-Attributes key holding the file name
      max_tracked_files: 1000      # in-memory backend only; 0 = unlimited
      entry_ttl: 24h               # sliding TTL per tracked file; 0 = no expiry
      stale_checkpoint: reject     # "reject" (default) | "reset"
      on_error: degrade            # "degrade" (default) | "fail"
```

- **`storage`** — ID of any
  [storage extension](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/exporter/redisexporter#storage-extension).
  When set, checkpoints are persisted through that extension's client and shared across all
  replicas (the right choice for scaled deployments). When unset, checkpoints live in process
  memory, which is only safe for single-replica deployments — the receiver logs a warning at
  start in that case.
- **`file_attribute`** — the key in the `X-Common-Attributes` header that holds the delivered
  file's name (e.g. `somelocation/somefile.gz`). It is used verbatim as part of the checkpoint
  key.
- **`max_tracked_files`** — caps the number of tracked files in the in-memory backend (least
  recently updated are evicted first); `0` means unlimited.
- **`entry_ttl`** — the sliding time-to-live of a checkpoint entry: an entry not updated within
  this duration expires and the next delivery is processed from line 1. `0` means entries never
  expire.
- **`stale_checkpoint`** — what happens when a resent file ends *before* its recorded checkpoint
  (the file was shrunk or truncated, or it is a different file reusing the name):
  - `reject` (default): the receiver responds `400 Bad Request`; the entry expires with
    `entry_ttl` (or on restart, in in-memory mode).
  - `reset`: the receiver clears the entry and responds `503 Service Unavailable`, so the
    sender's retry is processed as a fresh delivery from line 1.
- **`on_error`** — what happens when the checkpoint store is unavailable mid-delivery:
  - `degrade` (default): the delivery continues untracked; at-least-once is preserved.
  - `fail`: the receiver responds `503 Service Unavailable`, so the sender can retry.

Semantics:

- A checkpoint only advances after a batch has been forwarded successfully — a failed delivery
  never advances the shared checkpoint.
- Retrying after a failed delivery re-sends already-exported lines (at-least-once: possible
  duplication, never loss).
- A resend that carries no lines beyond the recorded checkpoint is a no-op delivery: the
  receiver responds `200 OK` without forwarding or unmarshaling anything (the already-exported
  prefix is skipped and the checkpoint is left unchanged).
- While file tracking is enabled, each forwarded **log** record is additionally stamped with a
  `file.line` record attribute carrying its 1-based line number within the delivered file.
  Together with the `file.path` resource attribute, records carry an absolute (file, line)
  coordinate, continuous across split deliveries. If a batch cannot be mapped 1-to-1 onto
  source lines (e.g. one line decodes into several records), it is still forwarded, but the
  affected records simply lack `file.line`. The relevant telemetry signals are documented in
  [documentation.md](documentation.md).

## Encodings

Any encoding extension can be used with this receiver. There are additionally built-in encodings, which are deprecated.
In the future it will be required to specify an encoding extension, and the built-in encodings will be removed.

### cwmetrics (deprecated)

The built-in `cwmetrics` encoding is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
Use the [`awscloudwatchmetricstreams_encoding`](../../extension/encoding/awscloudwatchmetricstreamsencodingextension)
extension with `format: json` instead.

```yaml
extensions:
  awscloudwatchmetricstreams_encoding:
    format: json
receivers:
  httplogs:
    encoding: awscloudwatchmetricstreams_encoding
```

### cwlogs (deprecated)

The built-in `cwlogs` encoding is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
Use the [`aws_logs_encoding`](../../extension/encoding/awslogsencodingextension) extension with
`format: cloudwatch` instead.

```yaml
extensions:
  aws_logs_encoding:
    format: cloudwatch
receivers:
  httplogs:
    encoding: aws_logs_encoding
```

### otlp\_v1 (deprecated)

The built-in `otlp_v1` encoding is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
Use the [`awscloudwatchmetricstreams_encoding`](../../extension/encoding/awscloudwatchmetricstreamsencodingextension)
extension with `format: opentelemetry1.0` instead.

```yaml
extensions:
  awscloudwatchmetricstreams_encoding:
    format: opentelemetry1.0
receivers:
  httplogs:
    encoding: awscloudwatchmetricstreams_encoding
```
